methods.label: Use a small signed remainder
methods.explanation:
A useful small power is \(2^6=64=5\cdot13-1\), so
\[
2^6\equiv-1\pmod{13}.
\]
Here congruence modulo \(13\) means that the two numbers differ by a multiple of \(13\). Replacing factors by congruent numbers preserves the remainder of their product.

Since \(1000=6\cdot166+4\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
2^{1000}
&=(2^6)^{166}2^4\\
&\equiv(-1)^{166}\cdot16\\
&=16\equiv3\pmod{13}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(0\le3<13\), the remainder is \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: A directly computed small power and elementary exponent laws reduce the large exponent; no exponent theorem is needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: Reducing a large power modulo an integer is the specific target. Congruence and remainder arithmetic support replacing factors, while exponent-sum and power-of-power laws justify the decomposition of 2¹⁰⁰⁰.
